CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  April 16, 2025-8:30 A.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING WITH
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY SUPERVISOR KATHRYN BARGER
OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called to order the special joint meeting with Los
  Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger at 8:44 a.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Supervisor Barger.
ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton (absent)
  Councilmember Justin Jones (absent)
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michete Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  STATUS UPDATE REGARDING COORDINATED EFFORTS
  WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY ON EATON FIRE RECOVERY

  City Manager Marquez reported on the Eaton Fire that occurred
  in January 2025 and the collaborative efforts between the City
  and Los Angeles County during the fire and to provide relief and
  assistance to impacted residents as part of a coordinated
  recovery.

  In response to Councilmember Cole's comments regarding the
  need to collaborate with the County's Public Works department
  to restore safe water infrastructure, Supervisor Barger reported
  that the County is working with the State to request federal
  funding to rebuild the water districts affected by the Eaton Fire.

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, advocated for the release of
  information/local government agency reports on each
  entities response to the Eaton Fire.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus
  of the City Council, the information was received and filed.

Council Minutes  1  04/16/2025
   STATUS UPDATE ON CITY AND COUNTY
  COLLABORATIVE EFFORTS RELATED TO THE PROPOSED
  MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENT OF THE "KAISER" PROPERTY
  AT 434-470 NORTH LAKE AVENUE, PASADENA, CA

  David Klug, Economic Development Director, presented a
  Powerpoint presentation on the Kaiser Property Project,
  providing background information on the project, a timeline of
  events, community outreach efforts, the Surplus Lands Act
  evaluation, and projected next steps of the project.

  Vice Mayor Rivas and Supervisor Barger thanked City staff for
  organizing the community meetings and noted that such
  meetings are important to keep the public informed and receive
  quality feedback.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus
  of the City Council, the information was received and filed.

  UPDATE ON PLANNING FOR LOS ANGELES 2028
  OLYMPICS AND PARALYMPICS GAMES (LA28)

  Alex Souto, Deputy City Manager, provided a Powerpoint
  presentation on the City's planning process for the upcoming Los
  Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic games. He presented
  information on tourism planning, economic development
  initiatives, public safety components, and sustainable energy
  planning.

  Councilmember Madison expressed excitement for the 2028
  Olympic Games to be held throughout Los Angeles. In response
  to Councilmember Masuda's inquiry, Vie Knoll, Director of Venue
  City Relations - LA28, clarified that information on contracts is
  not made public until venues are finalized and approved by the
  International Olympic Committee (IOC).

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus
  of the City Council, the information was received and filed.

  INFORMATION ON MEASURE A HOMELESS FUNDING

  Jim Wong, Housing Director, provided introductory comments
  on the item; Marco Santana, Homeless Initiative - LA County,
  reported on Measure A and the local solutions funds, and the
  new requirements and oversight of spending Measure A dollars.

Council Minutes  2  04/16/2025
   Discussion ensued regarding coordination with the Burbank-
  Glendale-Pasadena Housing Trust and the San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Governments ("SGVCOG") Housing Trust to allocate
  funding for affordable housing.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding the
  recent budget cuts for homelessness funding, Mr. Santana
  reported that the County's traditional spending on
  comprehensive homeless services decreased due to
  disbursement of funds to other categories. He noted that despite
  the decrease in traditional funding, the Measure A funding and
  the $300 million allocated for LACAHSA (LA County Affordable
  Housing Solutions Agency) allows for an overall increase of
  funding for homeless services and affordable housing projects.
  Supervisor Barger also stated the need for auditing of funds and
  expenditures to ensure appropriate and effective usage of funds.

  In response to Councilmember Lyon's inquiry regarding the
  movements of unhoused individuals throughout the County, Mr.
  Santana reported that the County has created a manual for
  jurisdictions to follow and use as aguide in response to the
  Grants Pass decision, and he noted that the County utilizes the
  Pathway Home approach to get unhoused individuals off of the
  streets, place them into interim housing, and provide guidance.

  Councilmember Madison expressed his concerns regarding
  recent incidents at Metro stations, and Mayor Gordo advocated
  for the City to have a coordinated comprehensive approach with
  Metro law enforcement and Pasadena Police Department, and
  requested that LA County consider funding additional H.O.P.E.
  teams and/or officers to improve public safety at these stations
  and surrounding areas.

  Councilmember Cole advocated for the City to adopt the
  SGVCOG's good neighbor policy, ensuring that cities take
  responsibility to help the unhoused individuals in their own
  jurisdictions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that one letter was received by the
  City Clerk's Office advocating for Supervisor Barger and the City
  Council to work with local nonprofit organizations to fund a motel
  lease program, create interim housing projects, and/or motel
  conversion projects, which was distributed to the City Council
  and Supervisor Barger, posted online, and made part of the
  public record.

  Council Minutes  3  04/16/2025
   Allison Henry, Pasadena resident, advocated for the City to
  collaborate with LA County to discuss rental assistance and
  eviction defense to prevent homelessness.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus
  of the City Council, the information was received and filed.

ADJOURNMENT  Mayor Gordo thanked Supervisor Barger and her staff for their
  leadership and efforts to support residents of Pasadena,
  Altadena, and County of Los Angeles.

  Supervisor Barger expressed her deep appreciation to the City
  Council, City staff, and residents on their partnership and
  willingness to work with the County for the benefit of all residents
  in the area.
